system: You are Apple, an expert Roblox Luau engineer. Reply with exactly one fenced ```luau code block and nothing else.
prompt: Write a server Script for a door model that opens when a player triggers a ProximityPrompt and closes again. The door should not be able to be triggered again while it is already moving.

checks.why: A ProximityPrompt that is never connected is the Lemonade failure: parts exist, nothing happens.
ProximityPrompt has no Visible property. The untrained base invented one; it fails silently at runtime.
Re-triggering mid-swing is the single most common door defect.

system: You are Apple, an expert Roblox Luau engineer. Reply with exactly one fenced ```luau code block and nothing else.
prompt: Write a Luau function that opens a door by rotating it 90 degrees around its hinge, using only real Roblox APIs.

checks.why: Rotation has to happen through an API that exists.

apple-v2 emitted doorService:GetDoorByHandle(doorHandle) — a service and a method that do not exist. Trained on library internals, it wrote code belonging inside a framework that was never defined. This check exists to catch exactly that regression.
apple-v1 looped out seven of these. "Joint" is not a Roblox class.

system: You are Apple, an expert Roblox Luau engineer. Reply with exactly one fenced ```luau code block and nothing else.
prompt: A door should only open for players who own the key item. Write the server-side code that checks ownership and opens the door. A client asks to open it via a RemoteEvent.

checks.why: The check has to live on the server; OnClientEvent would put the decision where the attacker is.
Ownership must be looked up server-side rather than taken from the request.
Accepting the answer as a remote argument is the classic client-trusted-authority exploit: the client simply sends true.

prompt: Write a door that closes itself automatically three seconds after it opens, and is safe if several players trigger it at once.

checks.why: The modern task library, not the deprecated globals.
Bare wait() is deprecated and throttles unpredictably.
Several players triggering at once is the concurrency case the prompt names.
